chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from his father, from al-Walid ibn Sabih, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'What do you feed your family in the winter?' I said, 'Meat. So when there is no meat, then oil and butter.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So what prevents you from this Karkour, for it is a matter of something in the body, meaning the Musallatha (the trio).'

He (the narrator) said, 'And one of our companions informed me that the Musallatha is taken as a Qafiz of rice, and a Qafiz of chickpeas, and a Qafiz of broad beans, or something else from the seeds, then all is ground and cooked.'

key_terms.الْكَرْكُورِ: Karkour (a term for a nutritious grain/legume mixture)
key_terms.الْمُثَلَّثَةَ: The Trio (a specific mixture of three grains/legumes)
key_terms.قَفِيزُ: Qafiz (a traditional unit of volume measurement)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic dietary recommendation for winter nutrition when meat is unavailable?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) recommends 'Musallatha' (the trio) as a nutritious winter staple, highlighting its practical value when meat is scarce. This preparation, typically combining equal parts rice, chickpeas, and broad beans, reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on accessible, balanced nutrition for daily sustenance. The hadith underscores the importance of utilizing locally available grains to maintain health and energy during colder months.
